phase3_findings.description: test_env_non_json_fails_naming_section uses pytest.raises(Exception, match="result_masking"), catching any exception type instead of the structured validation error.
test_env_wrong_type_fails_naming_setting sets an entry with no words ([""]), not a wrong-type value, so the env-side wrong-type error naming the setting is untested.
MASKED_COLUMNS_ATTR records one label per column position so duplicate labels repeat in the note; mask_secret_columns returns the input frame or a copy depending on whether anything matched.
The entry-must-split-into-words rule is enforced twice (config validator and SecretColumnMatcher) with different messages; unmasked_columns accepts empty labels.

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (one Critical checklist failure: the withheld-values note is missing for an empty result)

This PR is not ready to merge, because a query that returns zero rows from a secret column does not tell the model that the column's values are withheld, which acceptance criterion 4 requires.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical
- VC-24: FAIL (critical) — When a query result has at least one masked column, the run_sql text the model reads ends with `SQL Lens withheld the values in these columns: <labels>. Tell the user these values are hidden; do not try to retrieve them with another query.`, with `<labels>` the masked labels joined by `, `. The line is present in full however long the result's CSV preview is. A result with no masked column carries no such line. [src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py:140] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json counts (criterion 4 matches claim). Main path conforms: run_sql.py:137-149 builds masking_note from df.attrs[MASKED_COLUMNS_ATTR] (set by masking.py:166 as str labels), text exactly 'SQL Lens withheld the values in these columns: <labels joined by ', '>. Tell the user these values are hidden; do not try to retrieve them with another query.'; result = preview + 'Results saved to file' + truncation_note + masking_note, so the note is last and is appended after the 1000-char preview truncation (lines 130-135), hence present in full. No masked columns -> masking_note=''. Split of code condition `if df.empty` (line 92) inside the read-shaped trigger: the empty branch (lines 93-115) never reads MASKED_COLUMNS_ATTR. mask_secret_columns (masking.py:157-167) sets the attr from df.columns even when the frame has zero rows, so `SELECT password_hash FROM users WHERE 1=0` yields a result with a masked column but result_for_llm 'Query executed successfully. No rows returned.' with no withheld line. No sibling criterion names this case (criterion 1 concerns values; none excuses omission). Alternative -> departure. Impact is minimal since no values exist to withhold, so low severity. Non-read-shaped branch (line 177) is outside the trigger as no result columns are produced.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)
<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py` lines 358-359: `test_env_non_json_fails_naming_section` uses `pytest.raises(Exception, match="result_masking")`, so any exception type whose message mentions `result_masking` passes; it does not pin the validation error the criterion expects. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py` lines 346-351: `test_env_wrong_type_fails_naming_setting` sets `[""]`, an entry with no words, not a wrong-type value, so a wrong-type JSON environment value naming the setting is untested from the environment side. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/safety/masking.py` lines 151-167: the masked-columns attribute records one label per column position, so duplicate labels produce a note such as "token, token"; the function also returns the input frame when nothing matches and a copy otherwise, which callers are not told. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/safety/masking.py` lines 127-148: the "entry must split into words" rule is checked both in `ResultMaskingConfig` and in `SecretColumnMatcher` with different messages, and `unmasked_columns` accepts empty or whitespace labels. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

The column label itself still appears.
- [ ] The built-in entry list is exactly these 31 — complete by construction: `password`, `passwd`, `pwd`, `passcode`, `secret`, `token`, `hash`, `salt`, `pin`, `otp`, `totp`, `mfa`, `credential`, `apikey`, `api key`, `access key`, `private key`, `encryption key`, `signing key`, `auth key`, `recovery key`, `master key`, `session key`, `one time code`, `verification code`, `reset code`, `recovery code`, `security code`, `auth code`, `sms code`, `backup code`.
- [ ] Labels split and match as the Desired Behavior's secret-word rule states. At minimum these labels are masked: `password_hash`, `PasswordHash`, `session_token`, `recovery_hash`, `pin`, `PINs`, `APIKey`, `api_keys`, `OTPSecret`, `password2`, `users.password_hash`, `access_key`, `encryption_key`, `verification_code`, `one_time_code`. At minimum these are not masked: `id`, `name`, `email`, `phone`, `last_login_ip`, `session_expires`, `Key`, `COLUMN_KEY`, `sort_key`, `zip_code`, `author_id`.
- [ ] When a query result has at least one masked column, the run_sql text the model reads ends with `SQL Lens withheld the values in these columns: <labels>. Tell the user these values are hidden; do not try to retrieve them with another query.`, with `<labels>` the masked labels joined by `, `. The line is present in full however long the result's CSV preview is. A result with no masked column carries no such line.
- [ ] The system prompt's "Data Confidentiality" section contains the line `- Select only the columns the question needs. Do not use SELECT * on data tables, and do not select columns that hold secrets, such as passwords, password hashes, tokens, PINs, keys or one-time codes.`
- [ ] An entry in `[result_masking].extra_words` masks matching columns in addition to the built-in entries, and is split into words by the same rule as labels: `phone_number` masks a column labelled `PhoneNumber`.
- [ ] A label listed in `[result_masking].unmasked_columns` is shown unmasked, matched without regard to case: `token_count` exempts `TOKEN_COUNT`. The match is on the whole label, so `token_count` does not exempt the prefixed label MySQL gives a duplicate column (`users.token_count`, or `u.token_count` when the query aliases the table).
- [ ] With `[result_masking]` absent from the config, the built-in entries mask matching columns and no column is exempt. No `[result_masking]` setting turns masking off.
- [ ] `[result_masking]` with an unknown key, a value of the wrong type, or an entry that splits into no words makes config loading fail with a validation error naming the setting, from TOML and from a JSON-valued `SQLLENS_RESULT_MASKING__*` environment variable. An environment value that is not valid JSON (for example `SQLLENS_RESULT_MASKING__EXTRA_WORDS=phone`) also makes loading fail, with an error that names the `result_masking` section. In every one of these cases `sqllens validate` exits non-zero.
- [ ] Masking applies in all four combinations of `database.read_only` (true or false) and `[[rls]]` (rules present or absent), and for answers produced by the `verify-memory` command.
- [ ] With `[[rls]]` rules configured, the agent still builds, and the RLS relation check still runs on the engine runner.
- [ ] A result the row cap truncated still carries the "Result truncated at N rows" note in the model's text after masking.
- [ ] The change leaves these cases unmasked: a secret column renamed by an alias, a UNION's first-branch label or a view (for example `password_hash AS h`); an unaliased expression whose result label the database builds without the column's name (SQLite labels `upper(password_hash)` with that text, so the rule masks it; how MySQL and PostgreSQL label each expression is not established); a PostgreSQL whole-row value (`row_to_json(u)`); a label whose words run together (`passwordhash`); a PIN-type or other secret column whose label holds none of the entry words (the label of the reported PIN-type column was not recorded, so whether the built-in list covers it is not established); values a database error message repeats; sampled values that catalog statistics views return. It also leaves contact columns (email, phone, IP, browser) unmasked unless an operator adds them, and leaves the INFO level of the model payload log in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py` unchanged.
